findings.title: retryCount cleanup deletes unrelated and already-scheduled reminders
findings.body: The cron deleteMany ORs past-due SMS reminders with retryCount > 1, and that second branch has no method, scheduled, or scheduledDate filter. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL, SMS, and WHATSAPP, so the next run of this SMS job deletes every row with retryCount > 1, including non-SMS reminders and SMS reminders Twilio already accepted (scheduled true, referenceId set). Losing referenceId means a later booking cancellation cannot cancel the provider message, and reminders this job does not own can disappear. Restrict the predicate to unscheduled SMS rows (method SMS, scheduled false, retryCount > 1).

findings.title: Any two errors permanently drop the SMS reminder
findings.body: retryCount is incremented in the catch that wraps the whole reminder, not only a rejected Twilio schedule. Profile lookup, booker URL, template rendering, or a DB error after Twilio already returned a SID all count as failures. After two such errors the next cron deletes the row because retryCount > 1. A short outage therefore discards every in-window SMS reminder instead of retrying until the event. If scheduleSMS succeeded and the following update threw, the catch still increments, scheduled stays false, and the next run can schedule a duplicate while the later delete orphans the Twilio messages. Count only definitive send failures, and do not increment once a provider SID exists. If the catch's own update throws, that exception leaves the loop, the handler never responds, and the rest of the batch is skipped.

findings.title: Missing recipient or empty body retries until the event
findings.body: retryCount is only updated inside the branch that calls Twilio. If sendTo is missing or the message is empty, the reminder stays scheduled false with retryCount 0 and is selected again on every cron run until scheduledDate is past. That is a permanent failure (no destination never reaches Twilio) and is exactly the infinite reschedule this change is meant to stop, while also keeping the job busy reprocessing the same rows. Treat that path as a failed attempt or delete the reminder.

findings.title: Overlapping crons lose retry increments and can double-send
findings.body: retryCount is written as reminder.retryCount + 1 from the value read at the start of the loop, not as an atomic increment, and the row is not claimed before twilio.scheduleSMS. This handler awaits Twilio and several DB calls per reminder, so a run can outlast the cron interval and a second invocation loads the same unscheduled rows. Both workers schedule an SMS and both write the same retryCount, so the counter may never exceed 1, the new delete never fires, and the attendee gets duplicate messages. Use an atomic increment and a conditional update (id and scheduled false) to claim the reminder before calling Twilio.

findings.title: No tests for retry limit or delete scope
findings.body: The new delete predicate and retryCount updates have no tests. Nothing checks that EMAIL/WHATSAPP rows and already-scheduled SMS rows (with a provider referenceId) survive cleanup, that an SMS reminder is removed only after two scheduling failures, or that a missing sendTo does not spin until scheduledDate. Those are the paths that drop reminders or fail to stop the infinite cron loop.
